measurement_contract: Hash the complete original upstream Git bytes before parsing. Reject drift, duplicate keys and missing files; never execute external TypeScript or Solidity.

For each published Gig Guard decision, require exactly one uniquely identified case, disjoint receipt IDs, exact purchase-to-archived receipt status and amount/Intent/epoch/settlement-miner match, and agreement of successful security evidence with recorded security purchase. Registration IDs and settlement miner IDs are different namespaces.

Separate recorded failures from no recorded answer; do not classify missing audited attempts as provider outages. Report answer availability per all recorded decision cases, not quality among successful answers only.

Never treat SHIP or a structured Secure/zero count as security clearance. Use a source-verified explicit self-reported missing-evidence contradiction diagnostic for the two Truvian regression fixtures. Report original app behavior separately; no claim FALSUM authored the app's existing guard.

The 12 planted labels were authored by a separate app team, not independent qualified AppSec gold. The 22 audited controls are not proven vulnerability-free. No cross-provider ranking, new paid inference, live settlement verification, external adoption or mission completion is implied.
source_selection: Two independently authored Season II mission 14 apps; all 12 original planted decisions and all 22 archived audited-v7 decisions; two Truvian explicitly documented missing-input regression examples selected after reading public records. Not a blind test or holdout.
